template.gone.cause.message: The server no longer has them ({{url}}). The demo may have been replaced by a newer one.
template.gone.cause.note: Error details, the cause under the headline machines:template.gone, on the line under it in the same place: what happened, and what the user can do. {{url}}: the missing file's address.

template.otherSnapshot.note: Error headline when a demo's snapshot on the server isn't the one its definition names (the demo was republished meanwhile). Its details are the line under it (machines:template.otherSnapshot.cause).

template.otherSnapshot.cause.message: The demo's snapshot on the server isn't the one its card names. The demo may have just been updated: reload the demos and try again.
template.otherSnapshot.cause.note: Error details, the cause under the headline machines:template.otherSnapshot, on the line under it in the same place: what happened, and what the user can do.

store.diskAttached.note: Error in the message bar when the user deletes a disk some machines still have (the Home page's Disks pane): the headline; its details are the line under it (machines:store.diskAttached.cause). {{machines}}: their names, comma-separated.

store.diskAttached.cause.message: It's attached to <name>{{machines}}</name>. Detach it first.
store.diskAttached.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machines:store.diskAttached, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything. {{machines}}: as that entry's note says.

resize.failed.note: Error headline in the Resize dialog (Home page, Disks: a stored disk's, a ramdisk's or an overlay's Resize…) when the resize is refused; its details are the line under it (one of the machines:resize.* causes).

resize.gone.message: The disk or overlay no longer exists. It may have been deleted in another tab.
resize.gone.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machines:resize.failed, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything. The disk or overlay being resized was deleted meanwhile.

resize.notResizable.message: Only a disk stored in this browser, a ramdisk or an overlay can be resized. A disk read from a URL or a file, or a blank disk, grows through its overlays.
resize.notResizable.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machines:resize.failed, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything. Resize was asked of a disk that can't grow by itself.

resize.unaligned.message: The new size, {{size}} bytes, isn't a multiple of {{sector}} bytes.
resize.unaligned.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machines:resize.failed, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything. {{size}}: the size asked for, bytes; {{sector}}: the multiple sizes are made of (512).

resize.notLarger.message: {{size, bytes}} isn't larger than the disk's size now, {{now, bytes}}. A disk can only grow.
resize.notLarger.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machines:resize.failed, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything. {{size}}: the size asked for; {{now}}: the size now (both as KiB, MiB or GiB).

resize.running_one.message: <name>{{machines}}</name> uses it and is running. Power it off first.
resize.running_one.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machines:resize.failed, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything. {{machines}}: the running machine's name; {{count}}: 1.

resize.running_other.message: <name>{{machines}}</name> use it and are running. Power them off first.
resize.running_other.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machines:resize.failed, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything. {{machines}}: the running machines' names, comma-separated; {{count}}: how many.

resize.inUse.message: A machine or a task (an export, a merge) has it open. Wait for it to finish, or power the machine off.
resize.inUse.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machines:resize.failed, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything. The overlay's or stored disk's lock is held by something other than a machine the store knows is running (an export, a machine stopping).

urlcheck.corsHint.message: CORS headers for this web app's origin: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with this origin or *, `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Content-Range, Content-Length, ETag`, and `Range` allowed in its answers to OPTIONS
urlcheck.corsHint.note: What a server must send for CORS, placed in the URL problems urlcheck.noAnswer and urlcheck.noPiece. Header names in backquotes stay as they are.

urlcheck.notUrl.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: what was typed isn't a URL.

urlcheck.https.message: The URL must be HTTPS. This web app is served securely, so the browser blocks plain HTTP from it.
urlcheck.https.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: a plain HTTP URL on another origin.

urlcheck.httpOnly.message: Only HTTP and HTTPS URLs can be disks.
urlcheck.httpOnly.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: a URL of another scheme (ftp:, file:…).

urlcheck.noAnswer.message: The server didn't answer, or answered without CORS. It needs {{needs}}.
urlcheck.noAnswer.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the request failed (the network, or CORS: the browser doesn't say which). {{needs}}: urlcheck.corsHint.

urlcheck.notFound.message: The server says there is no such file (404).
urlcheck.notFound.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the server answered 404 (for the image, or a chunked image's manifest).

urlcheck.noRanges.message: The server ignores byte ranges; it sent the whole file for a range request. It must answer `Range: bytes=…` with 206 Partial Content.
urlcheck.noRanges.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the server answered a range request with the whole file (200).

urlcheck.rangeStatus.message: The server answered {{status}} {{statusText}} to a range request instead of 206.
urlcheck.rangeStatus.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. {{status}}: the HTTP status code; {{statusText}}: the server's text for it.

urlcheck.hiddenRange.message: The server sends Content-Range, but CORS hides it from this web app. The server needs `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Content-Range`.
urlcheck.hiddenRange.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the range was answered, but CORS hides its Content-Range header.

urlcheck.suffixStatus.message: The server answered {{status}} to a suffix range (`bytes=-512`) instead of 206.
urlcheck.suffixStatus.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. {{status}}: the HTTP status code of a request for the file's last bytes.

urlcheck.preflight.message: The server refused a preflighted range request. Its answer to OPTIONS must allow the `Range` header (`Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Range`).
urlcheck.preflight.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the CORS preflight of a suffix range failed.

urlcheck.manifestStatus.message: The server answered {{status}} {{statusText}} for the manifest.
urlcheck.manifestStatus.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: a chunked image's manifest. {{status}}: the HTTP status code; {{statusText}}: the server's text for it.

urlcheck.badManifest.message: The manifest isn't a chunked image's: {{why}}.
urlcheck.badManifest.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the manifest (JSON) was read, but isn't a chunked image's. {{why}}: what's wrong with it (a message of its own).

urlcheck.pieceStatus.message: The server answered {{status}} {{statusText}} for the image's first piece. The pieces should be next to the manifest, where tools/chunk-image.ts writes them.
urlcheck.pieceStatus.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: a chunked image's first piece. {{status}}: the HTTP status code; {{statusText}}: the server's text for it. The tool's path stays as it is.

urlcheck.noPiece.message: The server didn't answer the request for the image's first piece, or answered without CORS. The pieces need {{needs}}, as the manifest does.
urlcheck.noPiece.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Home page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the request for a chunked image's first piece failed. {{needs}}: urlcheck.corsHint.

urlcheck.slow.message: The guest reads the disk over the network as it needs it. What it reads is cached in this browser, so later boots read that part from here. A chunked image whose manifest lists a boot's reads (tools/disk-trace.ts) boots the first time about as fast as a file. To keep the whole disk, download the image and add it with <ui>Add a disk…</ui> › <ui>A file, copied into this browser</ui>.
urlcheck.slow.note: Note beside a URL disk (Home page, Disks tab) and after a URL checks out in Add a disk: how a disk over the network is read. The tool's path stays as it is. The <ui> marker frames the Add a disk menu path as the page's element.

MachinesPage.state.running.note: Home page: a machine's state, in the list of machines (after its disks) and beside its name at the top of its pane. Here: it runs (in this tab or another).

MachinesPage.state.suspended.note: Home page: a machine's state, in the list of machines (after its disks) and beside its name at the top of its pane. Here: it has a suspended copy (Start resumes it).

MachinesPage.state.off.note: Home page: a machine's state, in the list of machines (after its disks) and beside its name at the top of its pane. Here: it is off.

MachinesPage.otherTab.message: The machine is running in another tab. Power it off there first.
MachinesPage.otherTab.note: Home page: message bar text (also an error headline) when an edit that needs a machine off finds it running in another tab.

MachinesPage.powerOff.confirm.message: Forcibly power off <name>{{name}}</name> to make this change? Unsaved work in the guest will be lost.
MachinesPage.powerOff.confirm.note: Home page: confirmation dialog's text before an edit that needs the machine on this page off (e.g. on the Disks tab). {{name}}: the machine.

MachinesPage.powerOff.ok.note: Home page: the confirm button of MachinesPage.powerOff.confirm's dialog.

machine-edit.saving.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: Save on the Settings tab, or a Connect at start box.

machine-edit.orphans.confirm.message: Save these settings? They change the hardware the guest sees, so the machine's snapshots will no longer be restorable. They will remain, marked as orphaned, until you delete them.
machine-edit.orphans.confirm.note: Home page, Settings tab: confirmation dialog's text when Save changes the machine's shape and it has snapshots.

SaveRow.save.note: Home page: the button that saves a machine's settings (Settings, Network, USB and Shared folders tabs), and the confirm button of machine-edit.orphans.confirm's dialog.

KeyboardField.keyboard.matched.message: This browser's keyboard looks like {{layout}}. <ui>Save</ui> to use it.
KeyboardField.keyboard.matched.note: Home page, Settings tab: note under the Keyboard layout after Match this browser found the layout. {{layout}}: the layout's name (a keyboard message). <ui>Save</ui> is the tab's Save button.

KeyboardField.keyboard.unknown.message: This browser didn't report a layout from the list. Only Chromium-based browsers report one. Choose your layout from the list.
KeyboardField.keyboard.unknown.note: Home page, Settings tab: note under the Keyboard layout after Match this browser found none.

MachinePane.busy.exporting.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: Export the definition.

MachinesNav.busy.importing.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: Import a definition….

MachinesNav.imported.toPick.message: <name>{{name}}</name> was created. You will be asked to select its disk files when it first starts: <name>{{files}}</name>.
MachinesNav.imported.toPick.note: Home page: message bar text after Import a definition… (or a template in the New machine dialog) made a machine with disks that are files on the user's computer. {{name}}: the new machine; {{files}}: the files' names, comma-separated.

MachinePane.delete.confirm.message: Delete <name>{{name}}</name>? This will delete its snapshots, its firmware settings, and its suspended state, if any. Its disks and their overlays will remain stored in this browser.
MachinePane.delete.confirm.note: Home page: confirmation dialog's text after a machine's Delete button. {{name}}: the machine.

MachinePane.delete.ok.note: Home page: the confirm button of MachinePane.delete.confirm's dialog.

MachinePane.busy.deleting.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: deleting a machine or a connection.

AdapterCard.adapter.move.message: Move the adapter. The guest numbers its adapters (eth0, eth1…) in this order, and its default route goes through the first one that reaches the internet. A machine running in this tab restarts when you save.
AdapterCard.adapter.move.note: Home page, Network tab: tooltip of each adapter's move up and move down buttons.

connection-kind.tailnet.note: Home page, Connections: what kind of connection it is, in each connection's line (and after an adapter's connection on the Network tab). {{host}}: its control server's host name.

connection-kind.local.note: Home page, Connections: what kind of connection it is, in each connection's line (and after an adapter's connection on the Network tab). Here: the local helper program.

connection-kind.room.note: Home page, Connections: what kind of connection it is, in each connection's line (and after an adapter's connection on the Network tab). Here: a peer-to-peer room.

connection-kind.tailcatExit.note: Home page, Connections: what kind of connection it is, in each connection's line (and after an adapter's connection on the Network tab). Here: tailcat that goes out through a server.

connection-kind.tailcatServe.note: Home page, Connections: what kind of connection it is, in each connection's line (and after an adapter's connection on the Network tab). Here: tailcat that lets clients in.

connection-kind.ephemeral.note: Home page, Connections: what kind of connection it is, in each connection's line (and after an adapter's connection on the Network tab). An ephemeral connection's kind; {{kind}}: one of the kinds above.

ConnectionsPane.connection.here.note: Home page, Connections: who has the connection now, in each connection's line. Here: an adapter of the machine in this tab.

ConnectionsPane.connection.otherTab.note: Home page, Connections: who has the connection now, in each connection's line. Here: a machine in another tab.

ConnectionsPane.connection.unused.note: Home page, Connections: who has the connection now, in each connection's line. Here: no one.

ConnectionsPane.logout.confirm.message: Log out of <name>{{name}}</name>? This will remove its node from the tailnet and delete its keys from this browser. Connecting again will log in as a new node.
ConnectionsPane.logout.confirm.note: Home page, Connections: confirmation dialog's text after a connection's Log out button. {{name}}: the connection.

ConnectionsPane.logout.ok.note: Home page, Connections: the confirm button of ConnectionsPane.logout.confirm's dialog.

ConnectionsPane.busy.loggingOut.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: a connection's Log out.

UsbSwitch.usb.title.message: Give the machine an xHCI USB controller with four connectors, each USB 2 and USB 3, for its USB devices.
UsbSwitch.usb.title.note: Home page, Settings and USB tabs: tooltip of the USB controller box.

UsbSwitch.usb.note: Home page, Settings and USB tabs: the label of the box that gives the machine a USB controller.

UsbSwitch.usb.orphans.on.message: Turning the USB controller on changes the hardware the guest sees. Once you save, snapshots taken before can no longer be restored; they remain, marked as orphaned, until you delete them.
UsbSwitch.usb.orphans.on.note: Home page, Settings and USB tabs: warning under the USB controller box once it is ticked (not saved yet); only for a machine with snapshots.

UsbSwitch.usb.orphans.off.message: Turning the USB controller off changes the hardware the guest sees. Once you save, snapshots taken before can no longer be restored; they remain, marked as orphaned, until you delete them.
UsbSwitch.usb.orphans.off.note: Home page, Settings and USB tabs: warning under the USB controller box once it is unticked (not saved yet); only for a machine with snapshots.

SettingsTab.vulkan.title.message: Give the guest Vulkan through Venus, alongside 3D. Its Vulkan programs draw with this browser's WebGPU, and what the guest is offered follows your computer's GPU. This is experimental, and snapshots can't be taken while a program uses Vulkan.
SettingsTab.vulkan.title.note: Home page, Settings tab: tooltip of the Vulkan box (shown with the 3D display).

SettingsTab.vulkan.note: Home page, Settings tab: the label of the box that gives a 3D machine Vulkan.

SettingsTab.vulkan.orphans.off.message: Turning Vulkan off changes the hardware the guest sees. Once you save, snapshots taken before can no longer be restored; they remain, marked as orphaned, until you delete them.
SettingsTab.vulkan.orphans.off.note: Home page, Settings tab: warning under the Vulkan box once it is unticked (not saved yet); only for a machine with snapshots.

SettingsTab.vulkan.orphans.on.message: Turning Vulkan on changes the hardware the guest sees. Once you save, snapshots taken before can no longer be restored; they remain, marked as orphaned, until you delete them.
SettingsTab.vulkan.orphans.on.note: Home page, Settings tab: warning under the Vulkan box once it is ticked (not saved yet), in a browser with WebGPU; only for a machine with snapshots.

SettingsTab.vulkan.orphans.onNoWebgpu.message: Turning Vulkan on changes the hardware the guest sees. Once you save, snapshots taken before can no longer be restored; they remain, marked as orphaned, until you delete them. This browser has no WebGPU, so Vulkan programs would draw nothing here.
SettingsTab.vulkan.orphans.onNoWebgpu.note: Home page, Settings tab: warning under the Vulkan box once it is ticked (not saved yet), in a browser without WebGPU; only for a machine with snapshots.

SettingsTab.vulkan.noWebgpu.message: This browser has no WebGPU, so Vulkan programs would draw nothing here.
SettingsTab.vulkan.noWebgpu.note: Home page, Settings tab: warning under the Vulkan box once it is ticked (not saved yet), in a browser without WebGPU, for a machine with no snapshots (SettingsTab.vulkan.orphans.onNoWebgpu otherwise).

DeviceSwitches.mouse.title.message: Give the machine a relative mouse (virtio-input) for the mouse lock's Raw mode. While the machine has the mouse, its motion goes to the guest unbounded by the screen, for games, at the guest's own mouse speed. Without it, the mouse lock has only the Pointer mode.
DeviceSwitches.mouse.title.note: Home page, Settings tab: tooltip of the Mouse box.

DeviceSwitches.mouse.note: Home page, Settings tab: the label of the box that gives the machine a relative mouse.

DeviceSwitches.touch.title.message: Give the machine a multitouch touchscreen (virtio-input), so touches on the screen reach the guest as touches. Without it, a touch moves the pointer and clicks.
DeviceSwitches.touch.title.note: Home page, Settings tab: tooltip of the Touchscreen box.

DeviceSwitches.touch.note: Home page, Settings tab: the label of the box that gives the machine a touchscreen.

DeviceSwitches.clock.title.message: Give the machine a clock device (virtio-rtc) that reads your computer's clock. A guest with its driver, in Linux 6.16 or above, gets a read-only RTC and a PTP clock that chrony can follow (refclock PHC), so its time stays right across snapshots and your computer's sleep.
DeviceSwitches.clock.title.note: Home page, Settings tab: tooltip of the Clock device box.

DeviceSwitches.clock.note: Home page, Settings tab: the label of the box that gives the machine the clock device.

DeviceSwitches.pointers.orphans.message: Adding or removing the mouse, the touchscreen, or the clock device changes the hardware the guest sees. Once you save, snapshots taken before can no longer be restored; they remain, marked as orphaned, until you delete them.
DeviceSwitches.pointers.orphans.note: Home page, Settings tab: warning under the Mouse, Touchscreen and Clock device boxes once one of them changed (not saved yet); only for a machine with snapshots.

DeviceSwitches.agent.note: Home page, Settings tab: the label of the box that has the page start its small program (the guest agent) in the guest at each boot, which sets the guest's clock after a restore and, if the box under it is ticked, shares the clipboard.

DeviceSwitches.agent.title.message: At every boot, $t(common:product.name) starts a small program of its own in the guest, which talks to the web app over the machine's vsock device.
DeviceSwitches.agent.title.note: Home page, Settings tab: tooltip of Run the guest agent.

DeviceSwitches.agent.on.message: The guest agent sets the guest's clock after a snapshot is restored, after a pause, and after your computer wakes from sleep (<ui-adjustments-horizontal>Preferences</ui-adjustments-horizontal> can turn that off). It can also share the clipboard. The guest must be running systemd version 256 or above. Nothing is written to the guest's disk. Changes apply from the next boot.
DeviceSwitches.agent.on.note: Home page, Settings tab: the note under Run the guest agent while it is ticked. Preferences: the Preferences pane's switch for setting the guest's clock. The <ui-adjustments-horizontal> marker shows the Preferences pane's icon before the word.

DeviceSwitches.agent.off.message: Without the guest agent, the guest's clock falls behind after a snapshot is restored until something in the guest sets it, and the clipboard isn't shared. Changes apply from the next boot.
DeviceSwitches.agent.off.note: Home page, Settings tab: the note under Run the guest agent while it is unticked.

DeviceSwitches.clipboard.message: Share the clipboard with the guest
DeviceSwitches.clipboard.note: Home page, Settings tab: the label of the box, under Run the guest agent (and off while it is), that has the agent share the clipboard with the guest. Ticking it may make the browser ask whether the web app may read the clipboard.

DeviceSwitches.clipboard.note.message: Copy and paste text and images between your computer and the guest's desktop. The guest must be running systemd version 256 or above, and either an X11 session or a Wayland desktop that supports the data-control protocol, such as sway or KDE Plasma. You can pause the sharing, or type the clipboard into a text console, from the <icon>clipboard menu</icon> in the toolbar.
DeviceSwitches.clipboard.note.note: Home page, Settings tab: the note under Share the clipboard with the guest (docs/plans/clipboard.md §5, docs/clipboard.md for the details it leaves out). Kept short on purpose: what it does, what the guest needs, where it's controlled. data-control is the Wayland protocol (ext or wlr) the emulator's agent needs; an X11 session: Xorg, or Xwayland under a desktop without data-control, through the CLIPBOARD selection; typing is the toolbar menu's Type the clipboard item. The <icon> marker's words are followed by the toolbar's clipboard icon.

DeviceSwitches.openrc.link.note: Home page, Settings tab: a link under Share the clipboard with the guest that opens a dialog with the command that installs the guest agent's service in a guest without systemd (one whose init is OpenRC).

DeviceSwitches.openrc.title.note: The dialog opened by the link under Share the clipboard with the guest (Home page, Settings tab), on how to run the guest agent in a guest whose init is OpenRC rather than systemd: its title.

DeviceSwitches.openrc.systemd.message: Clipboard sharing and setting the guest's clock after a restore both work through the guest agent. In a guest running systemd version 256 or above, the agent starts automatically at every boot.
DeviceSwitches.openrc.systemd.note: The same dialog: its first paragraph, what needs the agent and when it needs nothing from the user.

DeviceSwitches.openrc.run.message: In a guest that uses OpenRC instead, run this command once as root:
DeviceSwitches.openrc.run.note: The same dialog: the line over the command (a field with a Copy button). OpenRC is an init system, named because it's what the user may need to look up.

DeviceSwitches.openrc.what.message: This installs only the agent's service, {{service}}, which starts the agent at every boot. The agent itself isn't copied to the guest's disk; the service reads it from the machine at each start. To remove the service, run {{remove}}.
DeviceSwitches.openrc.what.note: The same dialog: under the command, what it installs and how to undo it. <code> is shown as code; {{service}} is the service's file, {{remove}} the command that removes it.

DeviceSwitches.openrc.close.note: The same dialog: the button that closes it.

SaveRow.saveRestart.note: Home page: the Save button's words when the machine runs on this page and the change takes a restart.

SaveRow.revert.note: Home page: button beside Save, while a machine's settings have unsaved changes: drops them.

MachinesPage.back.note: Home page: the button (and its tooltip) at the left of the top bar that closes the page and shows the machine again.

MachinesPage.busy.note: Home page: top bar, while an action runs. {{what}}: what it is doing (a `.busy.*` message of the pane or tab that runs it).

MachinesPage.dismiss.note: Home page: accessible name (aria-label) of the × button that dismisses the message bar.

MachinesPage.heading.note: Home page: its heading, for a screen reader only (the toolbar's Home button opens the page); also the name of its left column (a navigation landmark: the machines, the commands that make one, the browser's Disks, Shared folders, Connections, Preferences and About).

MachinesNav.heading.note: Home page: the heading over the list of machines kept in this browser, at the top of the page's left column.

MachinesNav.list.empty.message: No machines yet. The machines you create, or open from a disk image, are kept here, in this browser.
MachinesNav.list.empty.note: Home page: in place of the list of machines (under its Machines heading) while this browser keeps none; the buttons that make one (New machine, From a disk image…, Import a definition…) follow it.

MachinesNav.list.transient.message: opened from the address, not stored
MachinesNav.list.transient.note: Home page: under the name of the page's own machine (opened from the address, e.g. a test's ?machine=) in the list of machines.

MachinesNav.list.meta_one.note: Home page: under a machine's name in the list of machines, when it has one disk. {{state}}: its state (a MachinesPage.state.* message).

MachinesNav.list.meta_other.note: Home page: under a machine's name in the list of machines. {{count}}: its disks; {{state}}: its state (a MachinesPage.state.* message).

MachinesPage.state.here.note: Home page: a machine's state in the list of machines when it is the one open in this tab, off.

NewMachine.busy.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: the New machine dialog makes the machine chosen (empty, or from a template).

MachinesNav.newMachine.note: Home page: button under the list of machines that opens the New machine dialog (an empty machine, or one from a template).

NewMachine.title.note: New machine dialog (Home page): its title. It offers what a new machine starts from: an empty machine or a template.

NewMachine.empty.note: New machine dialog: the choice that makes a machine with the default settings and no disks.

NewMachine.empty.text.message: A machine with the default settings and no disks. Add a disk image or an empty disk to it afterwards.
NewMachine.empty.text.note: New machine dialog: the line under Empty machine, saying what it makes.

PreferencesPane.dropCaches.note.message: Right before a snapshot or <ui-zzz>Suspend</ui-zzz>, the guest agent has the guest's kernel drop the copies of files it keeps in memory, so the snapshot leaves that memory out and takes less space. The guest reads those files from its disk again afterwards, so it may be slower for a while. Only machines that run the guest agent (their <ui-settings>Settings</ui-settings> tab) drop their caches.
PreferencesPane.dropCaches.note.note: Home page, Preferences: the note under Drop the guest's disk caches before a snapshot. The guest agent: the small program the emulator starts in the guest, the Settings tab's Run the guest agent. The markers show the toolbar's Suspend button and a machine's Settings tab, each with its icon.

PreferencesPane.clockSync.note.message: The guest agent sets the guest's clock to your computer's when a snapshot is restored, after the pause of a snapshot or <ui-zzz>Suspend</ui-zzz>, and when your computer wakes from sleep. Only machines that run the guest agent (their <ui-settings>Settings</ui-settings> tab) can have their clock set. When this is off, a snapshot is a pause the guest can hardly tell, and its clock lags until something sets it.
PreferencesPane.clockSync.note.note: Home page, Preferences: the note under Set the guest's clock after a restore. AdapterCard.busy.disconnecting.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: an adapter's Disconnect.

AdapterCard.adapter.disconnect.note: Home page, Network tab: button on an adapter of the machine running on this page while its connection is up.

AdapterCard.busy.connecting.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: an adapter's Connect.

AdapterCard.adapter.connect.note: Home page, Network tab: button on an adapter of the machine running on this page while its connection is down.

AdapterCard.adapter.saveFirst.note: Home page, Network tab: on an adapter added but not saved yet, in place of its buttons.

AdapterCard.adapter.remove.title.message: Take the adapter out of the machine. A machine running in this tab restarts when you save.
AdapterCard.adapter.remove.title.note: Home page, Network tab: tooltip of Remove.

AdapterCard.adapter.remove.note: Home page, Network tab: button on each adapter that takes it out of the machine.

NetworkTab.adapters.none.message: No network adapters. The machine is offline.
NetworkTab.adapters.none.note: Home page, Network tab: in place of the list when the machine has no adapter.

NetworkTab.adapters.add.note: Home page, Network tab: button under the list of adapters.

NetworkTab.adapters.note.message: A machine can have up to {{max}} adapters, each with its own MAC address (eth0, eth1… in the guest, in this order). Adding, removing, or moving one changes the hardware the guest sees, so snapshots taken before can no longer be restored. You can attach, change, or detach a connection while the machine runs, like plugging in a cable. The guest's default route goes through the first adapter that reaches the internet.
NetworkTab.adapters.note.note: Home page, Network tab: the note under the list of adapters. {{max}}: the most adapters (4).

NetworkTab.netConfig.title.message: At every boot, $t(common:product.name) has the guest's systemd-networkd apply the settings each connection provides.
NetworkTab.netConfig.title.note: Home page, Network tab: tooltip of Take the connection's settings in the guest.

NetworkTab.netConfig.message: Take the connection's settings in the guest
NetworkTab.netConfig.note: Home page, Network tab: the label of a box under the adapters.

NetworkTab.netConfig.on.message: At every boot, $t(common:product.name) has the guest's systemd-networkd use each connection's MTU and search domain, such as MagicDNS's, and DHCP on adapters nothing else sets up. A tailnet's MTU is 1280; at the adapter's 1500, large packets can be lost. The guest must be running systemd version 256 or above. Nothing is written to the guest's disk, so the settings last until the guest shuts down. NetworkManager applies them by itself.
NetworkTab.netConfig.on.note: Home page, Network tab: the note under Take the connection's settings in the guest, while it is ticked.

NetworkTab.netConfig.off.message: $t(common:product.name) leaves the guest's network settings alone. The guest uses each connection's MTU and search domain only if it's set up to. From the next boot, none of $t(common:product.name)'s settings apply.
NetworkTab.netConfig.off.note: Home page, Network tab: the note under Take the connection's settings in the guest, while it is unticked.

FoldersTab.shares.title.message: Give the machine a virtio-9p device, through which the guest reaches its shared folders.
FoldersTab.shares.title.note: Home page, Shared folders tab: tooltip of the Shared folders box.

FoldersTab.shares.note: Home page, Shared folders tab: the label of the box that gives the machine the shared folders device.

FoldersTab.shares.orphans.on.message: Turning shared folders on changes the hardware the guest sees. Once you save, snapshots taken before can no longer be restored; they remain, marked as orphaned, until you delete them.
FoldersTab.shares.orphans.on.note: Home page, Shared folders tab: warning under the Shared folders box once it is ticked (not saved yet); only for a machine with snapshots.

FoldersTab.shares.orphans.off.message: Turning shared folders off changes the hardware the guest sees. Once you save, snapshots taken before can no longer be restored; they remain, marked as orphaned, until you delete them.
FoldersTab.shares.orphans.off.note: Home page, Shared folders tab: warning under the Shared folders box once it is unticked (not saved yet); only for a machine with snapshots.

FoldersTab.sharesMount.title.message: At every boot, $t(common:product.name) has the guest's systemd mount the shared folders, at their first access.
FoldersTab.sharesMount.title.note: Home page, Shared folders tab: tooltip of Mount shared folders in the guest.

FoldersTab.sharesMount.message: Mount shared folders in the guest
FoldersTab.sharesMount.note: Home page, Shared folders tab: the label of a box under Shared folders.

FoldersTab.sharesPath.note: Home page, Shared folders tab: the label of the field with the path where the guest mounts the shared folders.

FoldersTab.sharesPath.noteRunning.message: Mounting over a non-empty guest directory hides its original contents. A new mount point takes effect at the next boot. The guest must be running systemd version 256 or above. This feature works without writing anything to its disk.
FoldersTab.sharesPath.noteRunning.note: Home page, Shared folders tab: the note under Mount point, while the machine runs on this page.

FoldersTab.sharesPath.note.message: Mounting over a non-empty guest directory hides its original contents. The guest must be running systemd version 256 or above. This feature works without writing anything to its disk.
FoldersTab.sharesPath.note.note: Home page, Shared folders tab: the note under Mount point.

MachinesPage.empty.message: Choose a machine, or create a new one.
MachinesPage.empty.note: Home page: in place of a machine's pane when none is chosen.

StorageBar.storage.persisted.message: {{used, bytes}} of {{quota, bytes}} used in this browser. The browser won't clear it when space runs short.
StorageBar.storage.persisted.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Here: the browser keeps it when space runs short. {{used}}: the bytes the page uses; {{quota}}: the most it may.

StorageBar.storage.message: {{used, bytes}} of {{quota, bytes}} used in this browser.
StorageBar.storage.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. {{used}}: the bytes the page uses; {{quota}}: the most it may.

StorageBar.busy.asking.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: Protect from automatic deletion (the browser is asked).

StorageBar.storage.persist.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. A button that asks the browser to mark this web app's storage as persistent, so the browser doesn't delete it by itself when the device runs low on space. Shown only while the storage isn't persistent.

StorageBar.storage.persist.title.message: Without this, the browser may delete this page's machines, disks and snapshots on its own when the device runs low on space. This asks the browser to keep them until you delete them yourself. The browser decides whether to agree, and may do so without asking you; if it declines, this button stays.
StorageBar.storage.persist.title.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Tooltip of Protect from automatic deletion (StorageBar.storage.persist).

StorageBar.storage.clear.title.message: Delete the cached parts of URL disks. They will be read from the network again, by a running machine too. The cache is kept at most a week after its last use, and the browser may clear it sooner when space runs short.
StorageBar.storage.clear.title.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Tooltip of Clear the URL disks' cache.

StorageBar.busy.clearing.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: Clear the URL disks' cache.

StorageBar.busy.trimming.note: Home page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: Free unused disk space (the guest trims its filesystems, then its disks' changes shrink).

StorageBar.storage.clear.message: Clear the URL disks' cache ({{size, bytes}})
StorageBar.storage.clear.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. A button that drops the kept blocks of URL disks. {{size}}: their bytes.

storage-report.storage.shaders.note: An item of What uses the space, the list of what fills the browser's storage (Home page, at the bottom), before its size (StorageDetails.item). The shaders machines with Vulkan translated, kept so that a program's next start translates nothing again; shared by every machine.

StorageBar.storage.clearShaders.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. A button that deletes the kept translated shaders of machines with Vulkan. {{size}}: their bytes.

StorageBar.storage.clearShaders.title.message: Delete the shaders that machines with Vulkan translated. A program's next start translates them again, which takes longer. A machine running now keeps those it holds and stores them again as they change.
StorageBar.storage.clearShaders.title.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Tooltip of Clear Vulkan's shaders.

StorageBar.storage.trim.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom, shown while this tab's machine runs with the guest agent. A button: the guest's filesystems tell its disks which blocks they no longer use, and the disks' changes in this browser shrink by them.

StorageBar.storage.trim.title.message: Have the running guest hand back the disk space its files no longer use (it trims its filesystems, as fstrim does), so that its disks' changes take less of this browser's storage. Its disks pause for a few seconds while they shrink.
StorageBar.storage.trim.title.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Tooltip of Free unused disk space.

PreferencesPane.shaderBudget.note: Home page, Preferences: the label of a list of sizes (MiB), the most that Vulkan's translated shaders may take in the browser's storage.

PreferencesPane.shaderBudget.default.note: Home page, Preferences: the default choice of Vulkan shader cache size. {{n}}: the size in MiB.

PreferencesPane.shaderBudget.note.message: Translated Vulkan shaders are kept in this browser's storage so they don't need to be re-translated when any machine uses them again. When this limit is reached, the least recently used shaders are evicted first. When in use, they take about this much memory. Changes apply from the next machine start.
PreferencesPane.shaderBudget.note.note: Home page, Preferences: the note under Vulkan shader cache size.

MachinesPage.powerOff.confirm.soft.message: Shut <name>{{name}}</name> down to make this change? Its guest will be asked to shut down first; you will be able to power it off forcibly, if needed.
MachinesPage.powerOff.confirm.soft.note: Text of the question asked before an edit on the Home page that needs the machine off, when its guest's agent (the page's program in the guest) can shut it down cleanly. {{name}} is the machine's name.

MachinesPage.powerOff.ok.soft.note: The confirm button of the question asked before an edit that needs the machine off, when its guest can shut down cleanly.

resize.tooLarge.message: {{size, bytes}} is past the largest size a disk can be resized to here, {{max, bytes}}.
resize.tooLarge.note: Error details: the cause under the headline machines:resize.failed, also shown under the Resize dialog's size field as the size is typed. {{size}}: the size asked for; {{max}}: the largest size allowed (8 TiB, written as 8192 GiB); both as KiB, MiB or GiB.

StorageBar.storage.counted.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Shown instead of StorageBar.storage when the browser's count of the space used is lower than the size of the files this web app stores (the browser's count is out of date): the files' size alone, without the browser's quota. A warning icon follows it (StorageBar.details.behind.title). {{used}}: the files' bytes.

StorageBar.storage.counted.persisted.message: {{used, bytes}} used in this browser. The browser won't clear it when space runs short.
StorageBar.storage.counted.persisted.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. StorageBar.storage.counted, when the browser keeps the storage when space runs short. {{used}}: the bytes of the files this web app stores.

StorageBar.details.title.message: Show how much space this web app uses, and what uses it.
StorageBar.details.title.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Tooltip (and accessible name) of the info icon after the storage line; it opens Storage in this browser (StorageDetails.title).

StorageBar.details.behind.title.message: This browser's count of the space used is lower than the size of what this web app stores. Show the details.
StorageBar.details.behind.title.note: Home page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Tooltip (and accessible name) of the warning icon after the storage line, shown when the browser's count (navigator.storage.estimate) is lower than the sum of the files listed in What uses the space; it opens Storage in this browser (StorageDetails.title).

StorageDetails.title.note: Home page: Storage in this browser, the dialog the icon after the storage line (the bar at the page's bottom) opens. Its title.

StorageDetails.summary.message: This web app uses {{used, bytes}} of the {{quota, bytes}} this browser allows. {{free, bytes}} remains free.
StorageDetails.summary.note: Home page: Storage in this browser, the dialog the icon after the storage line (the bar at the page's bottom) opens. Shown when the browser's count agrees with the files this web app stores. {{used}}: the bytes the browser counts as used; {{quota}}: the most it allows; {{free}}: the difference.

StorageDetails.behind.message: This browser's count of the space used is lower than the size of what this web app stores. The count may be out of date.
StorageDetails.behind.note: Home page: Storage in this browser, the dialog the icon after the storage line (the bar at the page's bottom) opens. Shown when the browser's count (navigator.storage.estimate) is lower than the sum of the files listed under What uses the space; the three numbers follow (StorageDetails.behind.counted, .usage, .quota).

StorageDetails.behind.counted.message: Stored by this web app: {{size, bytes}}
StorageDetails.behind.counted.note: Home page: Storage in this browser, the dialog the icon after the storage line (the bar at the page's bottom) opens. A line of the numbers shown when the browser's count is out of date: the sum of what uses the space (the files this web app stores). {{size}}: their bytes.

StorageDetails.behind.usage.message: Used, as counted by this browser: {{size, bytes}}
StorageDetails.behind.usage.note: Home page: Storage in this browser, the dialog the icon after the storage line (the bar at the page's bottom) opens. A line of the numbers shown when the browser's count is out of date: what the browser says this web app uses. {{size}}: its bytes.

StorageDetails.behind.quota.note: Home page: Storage in this browser, the dialog the icon after the storage line (the bar at the page's bottom) opens. A line of the numbers shown when the browser's count is out of date: the most the browser says this web app may store. {{size}}: its bytes.

StorageDetails.items.note: Home page: Storage in this browser, the dialog the icon after the storage line (the bar at the page's bottom) opens. The heading of the list of what fills the storage (StorageDetails.item).

StorageDetails.close.note: Home page: Storage in this browser, the dialog the icon after the storage line (the bar at the page's bottom) opens. The button that closes it.

StorageDetails.item.note: Home page: Storage in this browser (StorageDetails.title). An item of What uses the space (StorageDetails.items). {{what}}: what (a storage-report.storage.* message, which marks the names in it); {{size}}: its bytes.

AdapterCard.adapter.names_one.note: The Home page, a machine's Network tab, an adapter whose room connection holds a registered name: its line of names. {{names}}: a list of one message (network:names-view.machine.*), the domain with its date, which marks the domain itself (so {{names}} isn't wrapped).

AdapterCard.adapter.names_other.note: The Home page, a machine's Network tab, an adapter whose room connection holds registered names: its line of names. {{names}}: a list of messages (network:names-view.machine.*), each domain with its date, which mark the domains themselves (so {{names}} isn't wrapped), {{count}} how many.

connection-kind.demo.note: Home page, Connections: what kind of connection it is, in each connection's line (and after an adapter's connection on the Network tab). Here: the project's public demo network.

MachinesNav.demos.note: Home page: button under the list of machines, between Preferences and About, that opens the demo store's page (machines ready to use, downloaded on a click) in Home's place.

MachinesNav.demos.title.message: Machines ready to use, set up and started in a click.
MachinesNav.demos.title.note: Home page: tooltip of the Demos button under the list of machines (between Preferences and About), which opens the demo store's page.

DemosPage.back.note: Demo store's page: the button (and its tooltip) at the left of its top bar that closes the page, back to where the visitor came from (Home, or the machine).

DemosPage.heading.note: Demo store's page: its heading, over the demos' cards (or a demo's details).

DemosPage.intro.message: Machines ready to use: choose one, and it starts in this tab where it was left, already set up, with nothing to install. What you change in it is kept in this browser, and the machine stays on the Home page.
DemosPage.intro.note: Demo store's page: the paragraph under its heading, over the demos' cards: what a demo is.

DemosPage.loading.note: Demo store's page: said while the store's list of demos downloads (a small file).

DemosPage.retry.note: Demo store's page: button under the error when the store's list of demos couldn't be loaded (the server down, the connection lost): loads it again.

DemosPage.unknown.message: This store has no demo {{id}}: it may have been replaced by a newer one. Its demos are below.
DemosPage.unknown.note: Demo store's page: warning over the cards when the link named a demo (?id=) the store doesn't have. {{id}}: the id in the link (short, lowercase).

DemosPage.skipped_one.message: {{count}} demo in this store needs a newer version of this web app, or is damaged, and is left out.
DemosPage.skipped_one.note: Demo store's page: a small line over the cards when the store lists demos this page can't read (a later version of the format, a damaged entry). {{count}}: how many.

DemosPage.skipped_other.message: {{count}} demos in this store need a newer version of this web app, or are damaged, and are left out.
DemosPage.skipped_other.note: Demo store's page: a small line over the cards when the store lists demos this page can't read (a later version of the format, a damaged entry). {{count}}: how many.

DemosPage.empty.note: Demo store's page: said in the cards' place when the store lists none.

DemosPage.notOurs.title.note: Demo store's page: the heading of the warning shown when a link opens another store than the project's (?store=), before any of its demos is shown or downloaded.

DemosPage.notOurs.message: This link opens demos published at {{host}}, not by the $t(common:product.name) project. A demo is a whole machine, set up by whoever published it: open its demos only if you trust them.
DemosPage.notOurs.note: Demo store's page: the warning's text when a link opens another store than the project's (?store=), before anything of it past its list is downloaded. {{host}}: the other store's server (its host name).

DemosPage.notOurs.name.note: Demo store's page: a line of the warning about another store than the project's, when the store gives itself a name. {{name}}: that name, the store's own words.

DemosPage.notOurs.show.note: Demo store's page: the button of the warning about another store (?store=) that accepts it and shows that store's demos.

DemosPage.notOurs.ours.note: Demo store's page: the button of the warning about another store (?store=) that shows the project's own demos instead.

DemosPage.from.note: Demo store's page: a small line over the cards of another store than the project's, once the visitor accepted its warning. {{host}}: its server's host name.

DemoCard.download.note: Demo store's page: a line on a demo's card: what choosing it downloads. {{size}}: the bytes.

DemoCard.mine.note: Demo store's page: a mark on a demo's card when this browser has a machine made from it.

DemoCard.older.message: You have an older version of this demo
DemoCard.older.note: Demo store's page: a mark on a demo's card when this browser has a machine made from an older version it replaces.

DemoStart.back.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: the link-like button at the top that goes back to every demo's card.

DemoStart.about.message: $t(common:product.name) runs a whole arm64 computer in this browser tab, with nothing to install. The demo downloads the machine as it was left running, and it carries on from there. It needs a recent computer, and works best in Chrome or Edge.
DemoStart.about.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: what the project is and what it needs, before anything is downloaded.

DemoStart.download.message: Starting it downloads about {{size, bytes}}. The machine's disk stays on its server and is read as the machine uses it, so the machine needs that server to run; what you change is kept in this browser.
DemoStart.download.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: what starting it downloads, and where its files are. {{size}}: the bytes.

DemoStart.needs.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: the heading over what the demo needs of the browser, each checked (machines:DemoChecks.*).

DemoStart.checking.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: said in the checks' place while the browser is asked what it has (a moment).

DemoStart.start.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: the main button: downloads the demo, makes its machine in this browser and starts it. Off when a check failed.

DemoStart.openMine.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: the main button (the default) when this browser has a machine made from the demo: opens that machine, as it was left.

DemoStart.fresh.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: the second button when this browser has a machine made from the demo: downloads it again into another machine, named with a number after it; the visitor's own stays as it is.

DemoStart.mine.message: You started this demo before: <name>{{machine}}</name>, last used {{when}}. Open it as you left it, or start a fresh copy beside it.
DemoStart.mine.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: said over the buttons when this browser has a machine made from the demo. {{machine}}: its name; {{when}}: when it last ran (its disk last written), a date and time.

DemoStart.mine.undated.message: You started this demo before: <name>{{machine}}</name>. Open it as you left it, or start a fresh copy beside it.
DemoStart.mine.undated.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: said over the buttons when this browser has a machine made from the demo, before its last use is known. {{machine}}: its name.

DemoStart.elsewhere.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: a warning when the visitor's machine from the demo runs in another tab of this browser (it must be stopped there to open here). {{machine}}: its name.

DemoStart.older.message: You have <name>{{machine}}</name> from an older version of this demo. This version starts as a new machine; that one stays as it is.
DemoStart.older.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: said when this browser has a machine made from a version this demo replaces. {{machine}}: its name.

DemoStart.runningHere.message: <name>{{machine}}</name> is running in this tab: opening the demo powers it off (you will be asked first).
DemoStart.runningHere.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: a warning when another machine runs on this page. {{machine}}: its name.

DemoStart.busy.download.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: said while Start the demo (or Start a fresh copy) downloads it and makes its machine.

DemoStart.busy.opening.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: said while Open my machine checks the machine's files are still on their server and opens it.

DemoStart.progress.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details: the download's progress, under its bar. {{done}}: the bytes downloaded; {{total}}: all of them.

DemoChecks.browser.ok.message: A Chromium browser (Chrome, Edge…), the browser $t(common:product.name) is made for.
DemoChecks.browser.ok.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: the browser is Chromium's (met).

DemoChecks.browser.warn.message: $t(common:product.name) is made for Chromium's browsers (Chrome, Edge…). In this one the demo may not work, or only in part.
DemoChecks.browser.warn.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: another browser than Chromium's (a warning: the demo may still run).

DemoChecks.isolation.ok.message: Shared memory for the machine (the page is cross-origin isolated).
DemoChecks.isolation.ok.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: SharedArrayBuffer is there (met).

DemoChecks.isolation.fail.message: The browser gives this page no shared memory, which the machine needs: its server doesn't send the cross-origin isolation headers.
DemoChecks.isolation.fail.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: no SharedArrayBuffer (the demo can't start).

DemoChecks.opfs.ok.message: Storage for the machine's disk in this browser.
DemoChecks.opfs.ok.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: the origin private file system is there (met).

DemoChecks.opfs.fail.message: The browser gives this page no storage for the machine's disk (a private window refuses it). Open the page in a normal window.
DemoChecks.opfs.fail.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: no origin private file system (the demo can't start).

DemoChecks.webgl2.ok.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: shown for a demo with 3D; WebGL2 is there (met).

DemoChecks.webgl2.fail.message: No WebGL2, which the demo's 3D graphics need. Check that hardware acceleration is on in the browser's settings.
DemoChecks.webgl2.fail.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: shown for a demo with 3D; no WebGL2 (the demo can't start).

DemoChecks.webgpu.ok.message: WebGPU, for the demo's Vulkan graphics.
DemoChecks.webgpu.ok.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: shown for a demo with Vulkan; WebGPU is there (met).

DemoChecks.webgpu.fail.message: No WebGPU, which the demo's Vulkan graphics need.
DemoChecks.webgpu.fail.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: shown for a demo with Vulkan; no WebGPU adapter (the demo can't start).

DemoChecks.memory.ok.message: Memory: this computer has at least {{have}} GiB, and the demo wants {{need}} GiB.
DemoChecks.memory.ok.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: the device's memory as the browser says it (met). {{have}}: GiB the browser reports (it says at most 8); {{need}}: GiB the demo's machine wants with the page's own.

DemoChecks.memory.warn.message: This computer says it has {{have}} GiB of memory, and the demo wants {{need}} GiB: it may run slowly, or the browser may stop it.
DemoChecks.memory.warn.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: less memory than the demo wants (a warning: it may still run). {{have}}: GiB the browser reports; {{need}}: GiB the demo's machine wants with the page's own.

DemoChecks.storage.ok.message: Room in this browser's storage: {{free, bytes}} free, and the demo needs {{need, bytes}}.
DemoChecks.storage.ok.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: the browser's storage has room for the download and the machine's first changes (met). {{free}}, {{need}}: bytes.

DemoChecks.storage.fail.message: This browser's storage has {{free, bytes}} free, and the demo needs {{need, bytes}}. Free up space on the <ui-home>Home</ui-home> page, whose bottom bar shows what takes it.
DemoChecks.storage.fail.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: no room for the download (the demo can't start). {{free}}, {{need}}: bytes. The <ui-home> marker shows the Home button's icon before its words.

DemoChecks.mobile.warn.message: This looks like a phone or a tablet: the demo needs a computer's memory and speed, and may not run.
DemoChecks.mobile.warn.note: Demo store's page, a demo's details, under What it needs: a mobile device (a warning: it may still run).

template.cutOff.message: The demo's download was cut off
template.cutOff.note: Error headline on the demo store's page when a demo's snapshot stopped downloading partway (the connection lost, a piece refused by the server). Its details are the line under it (machines:template.cutOff.cause).

template.cutOff.cause.message: The connection to {{host}} was lost before the whole download arrived. Nothing was kept: try again.
template.cutOff.cause.note: Error details, the cause under the headline machines:template.cutOff, on the line under it in the same place. {{host}}: the server's host name.

template.full.message: There's no room for the demo in this browser
template.full.note: Error headline on the demo store's page when the browser's storage refused the demo's snapshot (full). Its details are the line under it (disks:overlay.storageFull or disks:overlay.storageFull.numbers).

template.download.note: Error headline on the demo store's page when a demo's snapshot couldn't be downloaded for a reason the line under it says (its manifest isn't one, the server refused a piece, a piece arrived damaged): disks:chunked.malformed, disks:chunked.pieceStatus, disks:chunked.pieceWrong.

template.tooBig.message: This demo is larger than its card says
template.tooBig.note: Error headline on the demo store's page when a demo's snapshot on the server is larger than the download its card states (or past the most a demo may download): nothing was downloaded. Its details are the line under it (machines:template.tooBig.cause).

template.tooBig.cause.message: Its snapshot is {{size, bytes}}, more than the {{most, bytes}} it may download. The store may be broken: nothing was downloaded.
template.tooBig.cause.note: Error details, the cause under the headline machines:template.tooBig, on the line under it in the same place. {{size}}: the snapshot's bytes on the server; {{most}}: the card's download, or the page's limit when that is less.
